Why not? Here are some reasons.

  • Trust: New sites that work like Voat will take its users time and effort to trust the admins to moderate the way they're comfortable with.

  • Time: We only have so much time to shitpost in a day. The more clones there are, the more thin our attention is spread. At best, this would end up being one alternative among many on a list somebody posts when Voat goes down again.

  • Money: There are other free sites, even if they also are destined to die. Most people won't pay. There will always be image boards, at least. However, Voat's original model of user ads was a good idea, and it could still work.

  • Network effects: There are other clone attempts, and whichever happens to look most busy will probably be the most fun.

  • Technology: There are probably better ways to ensure freedom of speech on a forum, but some require extra steps, like installing some peer-to-peer network. We have the technology. We can build it better. If Voat holds out long enough, one of those alternatives might become popular. That means all the effort put into your conventional site would be made useless, especially if you haven't earned the trust of your users yet.

That said, if you focus on archiving your favorite content, to limit the initial scope of the site, and invite others to use it as a backup, maybe you could generate enough trust and presence to make it interesting.
